particle_model.title: States of matter and particles
particle_model.big_idea: Everything is made of tiny particles. Heating makes them move faster and spread further apart; the particles themselves never get bigger. When water boils, the bubbles are water vapour.
steps: Solid: particles close together, vibrating in place.
Liquid: particles close together but able to slide past each other.
Gas: particles far apart, moving fast in all directions.
Heating: particles move faster and spread out, so things expand. Each particle stays the same size.
Boiling: liquid turns into gas inside the liquid, making bubbles of vapour.
particle_model.sense_check: If particles grew when heated, a hot spoon would be made of bigger atoms than a cold one. Atoms don't change size like that.

steps: At 100 °C some liquid water turns into gas.

conservation_of_mass.title: Mass is conserved
conservation_of_mass.big_idea: When something dissolves, melts or freezes, no particles are created or destroyed, so the total mass stays the same. Dissolved sugar or salt is still there, just spread out too small to see.
steps: List everything you started with and its mass.
Ask: did anything escape (like a gas) or get added? If not, the total mass stays the same.
Dissolving: mass of solution = mass of liquid + mass of what dissolved.
Melting or freezing: the mass does not change, even if the volume does.
conservation_of_mass.sense_check: Evaporate salty water and salt is left behind. It must have been there the whole time.

worked_examples.prompt: 50 g of sugar dissolves in 200 g of water. Mass of the solution?
steps: Nothing escapes.
The sugar is still there, spread out.

worked_examples.prompt: A 100 g ice cube melts in a closed bag. Mass of the water?
steps: Melting changes state only.
No particles are added or lost.
